location.scope: new --manual-scaffold CLI flag + docgen-manual.md convention-file detection/parsing

issues.current: No mechanism exists for a human to contribute prose that survives regeneration -- the only external file the tool reads by convention today is the project's own source; nothing analogous to README.md/CHANGELOG.md exists for content the tool itself would ask a person to write.
issues.expected: `--manual-scaffold` writes `docgen-manual.md` with one heading per human-only User Manual section, each followed by an HTML-comment hint (`<!-- docgen-hint: ... -->`) describing what's known and what isn't. On a normal run, `docgen-manual.md` is auto-detected by filename (same convention tier as README.md/CHANGELOG.md) and parsed: a heading whose only content is the hint comment (or nothing) stays SCAFFOLD; any content outside the comment is real and renders with a MANUAL badge.
issues.description: This is what lets FAQ/Support/Customization notes/etc. ever contain real prose without the tool fabricating it -- and the real/hint distinction (content outside the HTML comment vs. not) is the part that keeps an untouched template from ever being mistaken for a filled-in answer. Implementation note: parsing is fenced-code-aware (a '## ' line or an HTML comment inside a code block is code, not a heading/hint), and --manual-scaffold writes with an exclusive-create open so it can never overwrite an existing file.
issues.rule_ref: chat design -- 'a file that survives regeneration, not something living inside the generated HTML'
